propositions: Compaction leaves the tracker working tree dirty with untracked SNAPSHOT.json, *.retired, and .tmp-event-* files because the write-retire-commit sequence has no rollback and runs in a detached background sweep without cleanup on worker death.

The next reconverge runs git merge origin/tickets; when a peer has already pushed those same *.retired/SNAPSHOT paths to origin, the merge must create files that exist untracked locally, causing git to abort with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge'.

The abort-only handler in _union_merge and push_recovery's untracked-blind recovery (git reset --hard tracked-only, git stash without -u) cannot clear untracked files, so every retry re-aborts identically, permanently wedging the store and stranding local commits off origin.

The fix detects the untracked-overwrite abort signature, parses the exact paths git names, relocates only those colliding untracked paths to a quarantine directory outside the worktree, and retries the merge once, keeping both parents and preserving all local commits.

Files moved to quarantine are only those git explicitly names as collision sources (regenerable compaction artifacts), while .tmp-event-* and untracked paths not named by git remain untouched, ensuring no loss of uncommitted event data.
A genuine content conflict or any failure other than untracked-overwrite still aborts, keeps local, and hints rebar fsck-recover, preserving the abort-only behavior for non-recoverable scenarios.
